newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore's IPC says able to meet Korean debts.
newsitem.headline: Singapore's IPC says able to meet Korean debts.

text.p: Singapore computer company IPC Corp said on Monday it was able to absorb the potential liabilities after its Korean unit defaulted on notes and added that any losses would not have a material impact on the group.

In advertisements in local newspapers, IPC said it faced potential liabilities of only Singapore $24 million for IPC Korea and not S$114 million to $224 million as suggested by some earlier local press reports.

Separately, in an interview with the Straits Times, IPC chairman Patrick Ngiam said the company would be able to statisfy the contingent liabilities in full from its existing banking facilities and internal resources.
"The potential loss of the Korean market for the PC business should not have a material adverse impact on the group as a whole," Ngiam said.
"I reiterate this point, I say it again and again, IPC Corp is definitely not going under."
IPC shares slumped to hit a new year low of S$0.41 in mid-morning trade on Monday before recovering to S$0.465, down 16.96 percent or S$0.095 cents. Volume was more than 13 million.
Last week, IPC Corporation (Korea) Ltd (IPCK) defaulted on repaying 570 billion won worth of promissory notes and the group said it estimated its Korean exposure at S$45.5 million.

Of the total million exposure, S$24 million came from contingent liabilities. S$15 million in accounts receivables and S$6.5 million came from the unit's paid-up capital. The contingent liabilities comprise guarantees given by the company in favour of banks and suppliers to IPCK.

"If the company has to write off its S$6.5 million investment in IPCK, treat the S$15 million accounts receivables as bad debts and accept the contingent liabilities of S$24 million, the company's profitability and net assets would be reduced," the company said in the statement.

"However, the Group's outflow cash position should only be affected by the potential contingent liabilities of S$24 million. The company is able to satisfy these liabilities in full from its existing banking facilities and internal resources," the statement said.
The statement also said no decision had been taken on whether to shut down its Korean operations.
It said an investigative team had been sent to South Korea after efforts to contact the chief executive officer of IPCK and other senior management failed.
IPC has a 92 percent stake in IPCK, with T.H. Kim, the CEO of IPCK and South Korean firm Samick owning the remaining shares.

It said its other businesses, outside of its PC operations, were expected to generate healthy returns for the group in the current financial year and reduce the percentage contribution of the PC business.

Among IPC's other businesses are original equipment manufacturing of computer motherboards and electronic components, production of point-of-sale terminals and electronic components, sale of interactive media services like video-on-demand and manufacturing of telecommunication equipment and devices.
